The test image shows a corn field with plants of notably variable height - several plants appear significantly stunted/shorter compared to normal ones, with some yellowing visible. This is a whole plant symptom.

Key features: stunted plants with shortened internodes, chlorotic/yellowing leaves, field-level view showing affected plants scattered among normal ones.

Top candidates for whole-plant stunting: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus.

Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma fits best: severe stunting from shortened internodes, chlorosis, plants significantly shorter than normal neighbors. Let me verify with one reference image.

The reference image for Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows late-stage fallen/dried plants with reddish coloration, which doesn't perfectly match. However, the test image's key feature is the field with clearly stunted plants (noticeably shorter) mixed among normal-height plants, with some yellowing — consistent with Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma's hallmark of severe whole-plant stunting from shortened internodes. The tropical-looking red soil setting also supports this (the disease is more prevalent in tropical/subtropical regions). The scattered pattern of affected plants fits leafhopper-transmitted disease spread.
